subject: Follow-up: data handling, log retention & next steps for Psi Analytics
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@psianalytics.com>, Ethan Boyle <ethan.boyle@psianalytics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: data handling, log retention & next steps for Psi Analytics

Hi Maya / Ethan — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and to capture the privacy/logging constraints you flagged. Please correct anything I’ve missed.

Key pain points you shared:
- Customer transcripts and generated outputs may contain PII (names, emails, phone numbers, account numbers).
- Legal requires demonstrable deletion on request and proof of redaction for covered fields.
- Current stack: ingestion via AWS Kinesis -> transformation -> stored in S3; real-time inference happens in your US account.
- Auditability: you need tamper-evident audit logs for who queried what and when (retention ~45 days preferred, but some teams need 90 day archive for investigations).
- You cannot accept plaintext token-level logs containing PII; redaction must be applied before long-term storage.

Success criteria you described:
- No plaintext PII stored in inference logs or long-term KV cache.
- Configurable retention policy per environment (dev/stage/prod), default 45 days with option for 90d archival on request.
- Exportable audit trail (immutable event stream + download) for compliance reviews.
- Pilot (private deployment / VPC) with <200ms median latency for typical short prompts and overall cost target in your range.

What Redwood can offer (summary):
- Private deployment option (VPC) so inference runs in your account/environment.
- Built-in prefix/KV cache controls and a redaction hook we can run pre-cache to strip or mask PII.
- Configurable retention windows and an audit-stream export (S3/CloudTrail-style delivery).
- Security checklist attached (redwood-security-checklist.pdf) + draft mutual action plan (redwood-mamp-draft.xlsx).

Open questions / items for Psi to confirm:
1) Preferred redaction approach: full-field redaction (remove entire field) vs pattern-based masking (e.g., emails -> user@[redacted]).
2) Which environments need archival beyond 45 days and who owns the archive access?
3) Required SLA (latency/availability) for the pilot vs production.

Next steps I propose:
- You send over your redaction spec and any sample transcripts (sanitized) — Maya mentioned attaching the internal redaction spec.
- We (Dev) will validate caching/redaction flow and provide a short tech note by EOD Thu.
- I’ll send the security questionnaire link and schedule a 30-minute technical follow-up next week to review the pilot architecture.

Thanks — Nikhil

--
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@psianalytics.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Ethan Boyle <ethan.boyle@psianalytics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling, log retention & next steps for Psi Analytics

Thanks Nikhil — this looks right. A couple clarifications from our side:
- Redaction must cover full names, email addresses, phone numbers, IP addresses, and account numbers. For legal we need evidence the fields were removed (audit metadata that shows redaction took place).
- Our preference is to remove the full field for account numbers and emails; for free-text we can accept deterministic masking if the original can’t be reconstructed.
- Retention: 45 days is ideal for the product team, but security has requested the ability to archive (read-only) up to 90 days for forensics — that archive must be access-controlled and exportable.

I attached our internal redaction spec (psia-redaction-spec.pdf) for your engineers.

Can Redwood do the redaction before writing any logs to persistent storage? Also important: prove deletion — does Redwood provide a deletion confirmation or tombstone in the audit stream?

Proposed time for the technical follow-up: Tue Jul 6, 09:30 PT — does that work?

Best,
Maya

--
Maya Singh
Head of Platform Security, Psi Analytics
maya.singh@psianalytics.com
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Psi - redaction + caching follow-up (internal)

Short note — looping in Dev to validate the following during the tech call:
- Confirm redaction hook can run pre-cache and strip PII before any KV entries or token logs are persisted.
- Show audit-stream events for redaction actions (who/when/what removed).
- Validate retention policy config per environment + archival toggle for security.

If Dev can prototype a small flow (local) we can show Maya on Tue and get an initial sign-off.

Cheers,
Grace

--
Grace O'Connor
Solutions Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@psianalytics.com>, Ethan Boyle <ethan.boyle@psianalytics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling, log retention & next steps for Psi Analytics

Maya — perfect, thanks for the clarification and the spec. Couple quick answers:
- Yes, our recommended pattern for your use case is to run the redaction hook pre-cache and pre-index so no PII persists in token logs or KV storage by default. We can demonstrate this in the tech call.
- We emit an immutable audit event for redaction/deletion actions (includes a tombstone id and timestamp) and can route those events to your S3 bucket or a security-only project.
- Archival workflow: we can configure an automated 45-day delete with an option to move to a read-only archive for 90 days; archive access will be role-restricted and logged.

Next steps:
1) I uploaded the Redwood security checklist and a draft mutual action plan to the questionnaire link here: https://redwood.app/sq/PSI-2027-07-security-questionnaire (attached files: redwood-security-checklist.pdf, redwood-mamp-draft.xlsx).
2) Dev will prepare a short prototype (redaction pre-cache + audit events) and Grace will lead the demo.
3) Let's lock Tue Jul 6, 09:30 PT for the tech call — I've added the slot: https://cal.com/nikhil/psi-nextcall-30m.

If that all looks good I’ll send a calendar invite and include a short agenda.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the next step.

--
